title: Finite coefficients admit prime-field extension trees
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme, $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring, and $F$ a constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaf on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-constructible-constructible]. Then $F$ has a finite prime-field extension tree in the sense of [def-v2-prime-field-filtration]. No curve or cohomological hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 03SC, second proof paragraph; Lemma 03RZ (constructible weak Serre property)

proof.text: The characteristic n=ringChar(Lambda) is positive because Lambda is finite, and its scalar multiplication annihilates the identity of every module sheaf. Prove the stronger statement for constructible sheaves annihilated by any positive n by strong induction on n.

For a prime-annihilated sheaf, forget its coefficients and evaluate the identity-annihilation equation sectionwise. Use the existing cyclic-module sheaf lift and then prime-coefficient constructibility transfer. Apply the prime constructor of the extension tree.

If n=1 then the identity is zero, so multiplication by 2 is zero and the preceding prime case applies, including zero coefficients and empty schemes. Otherwise choose a prime p dividing n, and write n=p*m. Positivity of n gives m>0; p>1 gives m<n.

Set phi=p*id, K=kernel(phi), Q=cokernel(kernel.ι(phi)). The sequence K -> F -> Q is short exact by exact_cokernel and the mono kernel inclusion. Kernel and cokernel closure make both outer terms constructible. Cancel the kernel inclusion to prove p*id_K=0. Since (m*id_F) composed with phi is n*id_F=0, its composite with the coimage projection is zero. Cancel that epimorphism to prove m*id_Q=0.
Apply the prime case to K and the induction hypothesis to Q, then the extension constructor. Finally specialize the induction statement to the positive characteristic of Lambda.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 03SC second proof paragraph and Lemma 03RZ. D2 replaces primary decomposition by strong induction on a positive annihilator, using the same kernel/quotient short exact sequence for a prime divisor.
